payload.title: Generic publish step: save, publish and unpublish Items to the Published* projection
payload.description:
## Goal
The generic publish step: promote an `Item` (draft) to the guest-readable `Published*` projection, and unpublish it. Today the only writer of `PublishedItem` rows is `content seed-edition` (it writes `Item` and `PublishedItem` side by side). This ticket adds the real state transition as one Python module used by the CLI now and by the editor Lambda (`PPY-3e5235`) later, with the same function projecting an `Item` for staging (`PPY-3e5e9d` mirrors it in TypeScript).

## Context (verified)
- Models (`amplify/data/schema.ts` L1581+ `Item`, L1750+ `PublishedItem`, `MediaAsset`, `PublishedMediaAsset`): `Item` has `lineageId`, `versionNumber`, `previousVersionId`, `versionState`, `versionCreatedAt/By`, `changeReason`, `contentHash`, `type`, `status`, `typeStatus` (`"<type>#<status>"`), `slug`, `section`, `sectionStatus` (`"<section-slug>#<status>"`), `title`, `headline`, `deck`, `byline`, `dateline`, `publishedAt`, `editionDate`, `sortTitle`, `pullQuotes`, `layout`, `editorial`, plus the four new fields from `PPY-44a0f9`. `PublishedItem` mirrors them with `sourceItemId`, `itemLineageId`, `versionNumber`; indexes `publishedItemBySlug`, `listPublishedItemsByTypeStatusAndPublishedAt` (`typeStatus` partition) are what the readers query.
- The only current projection code is `src/papyrus_content/seed_edition.py` `seed_article_records()` L223-410: `published_item_id(item_id) = "published-" + item_id` (L1208), `published-<media id>` for media (L318-370), `with_version_fields()` L1162, `content_hash_for()` L1183 (sha256 over `stable_stringify`), `slugify()` L1200, `to_aws_json()` L1196. Reuse these helpers (move them to a small shared module `src/papyrus_content/record_helpers.py` and import from both; `seed_edition.py` re-imports them, behavior unchanged).
- Python client: `src/papyrus_content/graphql_authoring.py` `PapyrusGraphQLAuthoringClient` has `get_record(model, id)`, `list_records(model)`, `list_by_index(index_name, key)` (needs `INDEX_DEFINITIONS` entries, L383+), `upsert(model, payload)`, `update_record`, `delete_record`; `create_authoring_client()` L857 (JWT from `PAPYRUS_GRAPHQL_JWT`, or IAM when running in Lambda, `graphql_http.graphql_use_iam()`). Item/PublishedItem/MediaAsset/PublishedMediaAsset are in `LIST_DEFINITIONS` L176-179, so `MUTATIONS` exist.
- CLI wiring pattern: `src/papyrus_content/cli.py` `PORTED_COMMANDS` (L204-231), `dispatch()` (L379+); `parse_options`, `resolve_mutation_apply` (`--dry-run`; writes are the default) in `options.py`.
- Decisions made here (YAGNI): (1) no per-version Item rows in Phase 2; an `Item` is edited in place, and each publish increments `versionNumber` on the `Item` and writes the same number to `PublishedItem`; `lineageId` = the first `Item.id`. History rows are a later follow-up. (2) `PublishedItem.id = "published-" + lineageId` (one row per lineage; the slug index stays unique). (3) Item `status` is `draft` or `published`. (4) Editions are untouched (Markus sites have none; Pretext edition membership stays with the seed/edition tooling).

## Exact changes
1. `src/papyrus_content/record_helpers.py` (new): move `content_hash_for`, `stable_stringify`, `to_aws_json`, `slugify`, `compact_dict` from `seed_edition.py`; `seed_edition.py` imports them.
2. `src/papyrus_content/publishing.py` (new):
   ```python
   @dataclass
   class ItemFields:
       type: str                      # "article" | "page" | any existing item type
       slug: str
       section: str | None
       front_matter_yaml: str | None  # raw YAML text, no '---' fences
       body_markus: str
       aliases: list[str]
       id: str | None = None          # None -> deterministic id (item_id_for) or new_item_id()
       source_path: str | None = None # e.g. "articles/foo.md" (importer)
       overrides: dict | None = None  # explicit column overrides (title, deck, byline, dateline, publishedAt)

   class PublishError(Exception):  # .errors: list[BodyError] | .code
   def item_id_for(section: str | None, slug: str) -> str      # "item-{slugify(section)}-{slug}" or "item-{slug}"
   def new_item_id() -> str                                     # "item-" + uuid4().hex[:12]
   def columns_from_front_matter(fm: dict) -> dict              # see below
   def save_item(client, fields: ItemFields, *, actor: str, now: str | None = None, expected_content_hash: str | None = None) -> dict   # returns the Item record written
   def project_item_to_published(item: dict, media: list[dict], *, published_at: str, version_number: int) -> tuple[dict, list[dict]]
   def publish_item(client, item_id: str, *, actor: str, now: str | None = None) -> PublishResult
   def unpublish_item(client, item_id: str, *, actor: str, now: str | None = None) -> PublishResult
   ```
   `columns_from_front_matter(fm)` (the Item columns are DERIVED from the raw front matter; the YAML string stays the source of truth): `title` <- `title`; `headline` <- `title`; `sortTitle` <- `title`; `deck` <- first non-empty of `deck`, `standfirst`, `description`; `byline` <- `authors` (list joined `", "`) else `author` (verbatim); `publishedAt` <- ISO-8601 UTC from `date` when parseable (ISO, `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `"Sunday, September 6, 2026"` style via `datetime.strptime` formats list), else `None`. `fields.overrides` win over derived values.
   `save_item`: derive with `derive_body` (`PPY-e169c5`); if `not ok` raise `PublishError`. If a record exists (`get_record("Item", id)`): require `expected_content_hash in (None, existing.contentHash)` else `PublishError(code="conflict")`; keep `status`, `lineageId`, `versionNumber`, `publishedAt` (unless overridden); update in place. New: `status="draft"`, `lineageId=id`, `versionNumber=1`, `versionState="current"`, `versionCreatedAt=now`, `versionCreatedBy=actor`, `changeReason="created"`. Always set `typeStatus`, `sectionStatus` from `status`, `bodyMarkus`, `bodyIr=to_aws_json(envelope)`, `aliases`, `metadata=to_aws_json({"frontMatterYaml": ..., "source": {"path": ...}})` (preserve unknown keys of existing metadata), `contentHash=content_hash_for({type, slug, section, frontMatterYaml, bodyMarkus, aliases})` (NO version fields in the hash). Write with `client.upsert("Item", record)`. Slug is immutable once the item has been published (`PublishError(code="slug-locked")`).
   `publish_item`: load Item (`PublishError("not-found")`); `derive_body` again (publish never trusts stored `bodyIr`); list its `MediaAsset` rows and require every relative `papyrus.images[*].src` of the derived envelope (not `http(s)://`) to equal some media row's `metadata.srcPath`, else `PublishError(code="image-missing", message=<the src>)` (a published article must never reference an asset the CMS does not have; to list the rows add `INDEX_DEFINITIONS["mediaAssetsByItemAndSortKey"] = {"field": "listMediaAssetsByItemAndSortKey", "partitionKey": "itemId", "fields": MEDIA_ASSET_FIELDS}` and query it by `itemId`); `existing = get_record("PublishedItem", "published-"+lineageId)`; version = `existing.versionNumber + 1` or `1`; noop (return `changed=False`) when `existing` and `existing.metadata.sourceContentHash == item.contentHash` and `item.status == "published"`. Build PublishedItem and PublishedMediaAsset records with `project_item_to_published` (same columns as `seed_article_records` L248-330: `id`, `sourceItemId`, `itemLineageId`, `versionNumber`, `type`, `status="published"`, `typeStatus="<type>#published"`, `slug`, `shortSlug`, `section`, `sectionStatus="<section-slug>#published"`, `title`, `headline`, `deck`, `bodyMarkus`, `bodyIr`, `aliases`, `metadata` = item metadata + `{"sourceContentHash": item.contentHash}`, `byline`, `dateline`, `publishedAt`, `sortTitle`, `pullQuotes=[]`, `layout=to_aws_json({"source": "cms"})`, `editorial=to_aws_json({})`; do NOT write the legacy `body`). `publishedAt = item.publishedAt or now`. Write order (re-runnable if interrupted): upsert `PublishedMediaAsset` rows, delete `PublishedMediaAsset` rows of this published item that no longer exist (index `listPublishedMediaAssetsByItemAndSortKey`, add to `INDEX_DEFINITIONS` as `publishedMediaAssetsByItemAndSortKey`), upsert `PublishedItem`, then `update_record("Item", {id, status:"published", typeStatus, sectionStatus, versionNumber, publishedAt, versionState:"current", versionCreatedAt:now, versionCreatedBy:actor, changeReason:"publish", bodyIr})`.
   `unpublish_item`: delete its `PublishedMediaAsset` rows and the `PublishedItem`; set the Item `status="draft"` and recompute `typeStatus`/`sectionStatus`. Idempotent (no PublishedItem -> `changed=False`).
3. CLI (`src/papyrus_content/publish_commands.py`, wired like `PPY-e169c5`'s command): `papyrus content publish --id <item-id>` or `--slug <slug> [--section <s>]` (slug lookup via new `INDEX_DEFINITIONS["itemBySlug"] = {"field": "itemBySlug", "partitionKey": "slug", "fields": ITEM_FIELDS}`; more than one match -> error asking for `--id`); `papyrus content unpublish ...` same selectors; `--dry-run` prints what would be written (record ids per model) and writes nothing; `--json`. Add `"content:publish"`, `"content:unpublish"` to `PORTED_COMMANDS`, branches in `dispatch()`, lines in `print_usage()`. Default actor: JWT `sub` from `create_authoring_client()` claims, else `"papyrus-cli"`.
4. `procedures/newsroom/tests/fake_client.py` (new, shared by `PPY-22a3b4`, `PPY-1d0f3d`, `PPY-3e5235` tests): `FakeAuthoringClient` with in-memory dict per model implementing `get_record`, `list_records`, `list_by_index` (partitionKey match for the index definitions above), `upsert`, `update_record`, `delete_record`, recording a `calls` list.

## Data shapes
Item after `save_item` (new draft), abbreviated:
```text
{"id":"item-articles-believe-the-rainbow","lineageId":"item-articles-believe-the-rainbow","versionNumber":1,"versionState":"current",
 "type":"article","status":"draft","typeStatus":"article#draft","slug":"believe-the-rainbow","section":"articles","sectionStatus":"articles#draft",
 "title":"Forty Billion Dollars Stopped Existing in Four Days","headline":"...","deck":"TerraUSD promised...","byline":"by various bots and Ryan Porter","publishedAt":"2026-09-06T00:00:00Z",
 "bodyMarkus":"There is an old [Skittles commercial](...) ...","bodyIr":"{\"schemaVersion\":1,...}","aliases":[],
 "metadata":"{\"frontMatterYaml\":\"title: ...\[LF]cover: assets/...\",\"source\":{\"path\":\"articles/believe-the-rainbow.md\"}}","contentHash":"sha256:..."}
```
`PublishedItem.metadata` = `{"frontMatterYaml": "...", "source": {...}, "sourceContentHash": "sha256:..."}`. Pending changes (UI badge) = `item.contentHash != publishedItem.metadata.sourceContentHash`.

## Tests
- Unit: `procedures/newsroom/tests/test_publishing.py` with `FakeAuthoringClient`: save new -> draft columns and derived `title/deck/byline/publishedAt` from the Pilobol front matter sample (`"Sunday, September 6, 2026"` -> `2026-09-06T00:00:00Z`); save existing with stale `expected_content_hash` -> `conflict`; invalid body -> `PublishError` carrying the derive error code and NO write; publish -> PublishedItem present with `bodyIr` equal to `derive_body(...)`, `versionNumber 1`, Item `status published`; republish with no change -> `changed False`, no writes; edit + republish -> `versionNumber 2`; media sync (add one, remove one) leaves exactly the current `PublishedMediaAsset` set; unpublish removes Published* rows and sets `typeStatus "article#draft"`; unpublish twice idempotent; slug change after publish -> `slug-locked`; interrupted publish (fake raises after the PublishedItem upsert) then re-run converges to the same final state; `seed_edition` tests (`procedures/newsroom/tests/test_papyrus_content.py`) still pass after the helper move.
- Gherkin: `features_backend/publish-item.feature` + `features_backend/steps/publish_item_steps.py` (steps use `FakeAuthoringClient`): "Publishing a draft makes it readable", "Unpublishing removes it from the published projection", "Republishing unchanged content does nothing", "A body with an unknown directive cannot be published".
- Sandbox smoke (AWS; read `AGENTS.local.md`): with `PPY-44a0f9` deployed to a sandbox, create a draft with `papyrus content import-markus` is not available yet, so use a REPL snippet in the PR to `save_item` then `poetry run papyrus content publish --id <id>` and read it back with `papyrus content list articles`.

## Acceptance checks
- `poetry run python -m unittest procedures.newsroom.tests.test_publishing procedures.newsroom.tests.test_papyrus_content -v` passes.
- `poetry run behave features_backend/publish-item.feature` passes.
- `poetry run papyrus content publish --id item-x --dry-run --json` against the fake/sandbox prints the planned record ids and writes nothing (check by `content list articles` unchanged).

## Dependencies
Blocked by `PPY-e169c5` (derive) and `PPY-44a0f9` (fields on the deployed API; unit tests do not need the deploy). Blocks `PPY-3e5235`, `PPY-22a3b4`, `PPY-fbb1fb`. Same-file conflicts: `cli.py` (also `PPY-e169c5`, `PPY-22a3b4`, `PPY-1d0f3d`, `PPY-085f79`: each adds lines to `PORTED_COMMANDS`/`dispatch`/`print_usage`; rebase, trivial) and `graphql_authoring.py` `INDEX_DEFINITIONS` (also `PPY-1d0f3d`).

## Risks
- Not transactional: the write order above makes publish re-runnable; a crash can leave a published row whose Item still says `draft` until the next publish. Documented, acceptable.
- Deleting `PublishedMediaAsset` rows needs the delete permission in the caller's auth (`editor`/`admin` have it; the Lambda gets it via `allow.resource`, see `PPY-3e5235`).
- Cached readers: after a publish, Pretext readers cache for 1 h (`READER_REVALIDATE_SECONDS` in `lib/reader-route-config.ts`); revalidation is `PPY-fbb1fb`.

## Needs Ryan
Nothing (the no-history-rows decision is recorded here; say so if you want version rows).

## Common rules (apply to every Phase 2 ticket)
- Work from a clean worktree of `origin/develop` (`git -C /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus fetch origin && git worktree add ../Papyrus-worktrees/<this-ticket> -b feature/PPY-b3a10e-<slug> origin/develop`). Never commit to `develop` or `main`; open a PR into `develop`; never merge to `main`. Conventional-commit messages. Update this ticket with branch, PR link and the verification output.
- `AGENTS.md` rules that bind this work: no backward-compatibility shims or fallbacks (clean breaks); backend tooling in Python unless noted; Pretext owns text measurement (do not measure DOM in React); read `AGENTS.local.md` before ANY AWS/Amplify/sandbox command; never run `ampx pipeline-deploy` locally (sandbox only).
- Note on language direction: Ryan's 2026-10-05 correction (epic comment 4174c5) says Papyrus is being ported from Python to TypeScript. Phase 2 follows the approved design in docs/standard-site.md (Python CLI/Lambdas + `papyrus-newsroom`). Keep new Python logic in small pure functions with fixture-driven tests so it can be ported; do not add new Python dependencies beyond those named here.
- Tests: Python unit tests are `unittest` under `procedures/newsroom/tests/` (run: `poetry run python -m unittest procedures.newsroom.tests.<module> -v`); backend Gherkin is `behave` under `features_backend/` with steps in `features_backend/steps/` (run: `poetry run behave features_backend/<file>.feature`); UI Gherkin is cucumber-js + Playwright under `features/` (run against a dev server: `npm run dev` then `PAPYRUS_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3001 npx cucumber-js features/<file>.feature`); TypeScript unit tests are `scripts/test-*.ts` run with `npx tsx` (add an npm script `test:<name>` in package.json).
- Install: `poetry install --extras "newsroom markus"` and `npm ci`. Verify `markus --version` prints 0.5.1 (PyPI `anthus-markus` 0.5.1 emits IR `schema_version: 1`).

- Notation: `[LF]` in this ticket text means a newline character (the board tool cannot store a backslash followed by n).
